subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Julia Hart <julia@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T14:15:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Julia (and Sarah),

Thanks for taking the time today - quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared starting point. I captured the pain, goals, and proposed next steps below. I attached a one-page recap and a compatibility checklist for your team to scan.

Pain points / triggers
- Cost: OpenAI + Anthropic spend has grown rapidly with embedding + generation workloads, looking for >=30% reduction in unit costs without degrading output quality.
- Latency & predictability: some production endpoints have variable tail latency during peak traffic.
- Vendor lock & flexibility: want the ability to run on open models (self-hosted or managed) and avoid being forced to specific proprietary APIs.
- Compliance: need audit logs, key management, and control over data residency for certain regulated datasets.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Primary generation: OpenAI (gpt-4o for high-value flows, gpt-4o-mini for lower tiers) + Anthropic for some safety-sensitive prompts.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings + small in-house FAISS service.
- Orchestration: lightweight orchestration layer that does model routing, retries, and simple function calling.
- Observability: Datadog traces + some custom token-level billing.

Compatibility & technical constraints
- API compatibility: need a drop-in path for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (prompt formats, chat messages, streaming, function/tool calling).
- Feature parity: function calling + streaming + structured output are must-haves.
- Model footprint: currently using multi-tenant hosted models; must support both hosted and private (VPC) deployment options.
- Security: KMS integration and audit logs are required for production.

Success criteria (initial)
- Unit cost reduction: >=30% per-token for generation/embedding in pilot workloads.
- Latency: 95th percentile within 15% of current SLA for key endpoints.
- Quality: automated evals show no significant regression on your prompt suite (we'll define pass/fail thresholds).
- Integration effort: PoC should take <= 4 weeks to validate with existing stack.

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama 2 70B / instruction-tuned variants (good fit if you want strong instruction-following with manageable infra).
- Mistral-Instruct family (competitive performance/cost profile).
- Falcon 40B / 180B variants (if you need stronger open-instruction performance).
- Smaller quantized variants for embeddings / high throughput endpoints.

Next steps (agreed on call)
1) I will send the compatibility checklist and the one-pager summary (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Sarah + engineering to validate function-calling and streaming behavior (proposed Fri 10:00 AM PT).
3) Proposal for a 2-week pilot (we provide dedicated capacity + monitoring) and a short evaluation plan (cost, latency, QA).
4) Security questionnaire (you said you'd share) - we'll start mapping controls to our Private offering.

Attachments: RIF_Discovery_Recap_20260712.pdf, redwood-compatibility-checklist.xlsx

If I missed anything or misstated priorities, please flag and I'll update the doc. Otherwise I'll book the deep-dive and share the pilot SOW draft.

Best,

Thanks Aditya - this is excellent and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority order: (1) cost, (2) data residency/compliance, (3) latency predictability. Quality parity is assumed but cost is the main driver.
- Timeline: if the pilot looks good, we want to move to a production rollout within ~3 months.
- Security: attaching our security questionnaire (LumenAI_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). We will need KMS + auditability documented for any private deploy.
- Evaluation: Sarah will lead the technical evaluation - she cares most about function-calling parity and the behavior of stream chunking for our real-time flows.

A couple of quick asks before the deep-dive:
- Can you provide a mapping of OpenAI/Anthropic API features to the models you propose (function calling, streaming behavior, limitations)?
- Any early cost estimates for the shortlist models by throughput (tokens/sec) would help set expectations.

I'll confirm the deep-dive slot after checking with Sarah. Thanks for pulling this together.

Julia
